painPoints.title: SIP Trunk Interoperability and Legacy System Integration
painPoints.description: AT&T Services faces challenges integrating Kandy SIP trunking with legacy on-premises PBX systems and third-party carrier infrastructure. Inconsistent codec support and signaling protocol variations create call quality issues and increase support overhead across their enterprise customer base.

painPoints.title: WebRTC Security and Compliance Complexity
painPoints.description: Implementing WebRTC-based communications within Kandy platform requires managing encryption, SRTP/DTLS protocols, and regulatory compliance (HIPAA, PCI-DSS) across customer deployments. Current security model increases operational complexity and slows customer onboarding.

painPoints.title: CPaaS Platform Scalability During Peak Messaging Volumes
painPoints.description: Kandy messaging component experiences latency and throughput constraints during high-volume SMS/RCS campaigns from enterprise customers. Current infrastructure requires optimization to maintain sub-second delivery SLAs and support multi-tenant isolation at scale.

opportunities.title: Expand Kandy UCaaS to Mid-Market Financial Services Vertical
opportunities.description: Target 200-500 employee financial institutions requiring embedded communications (voice, video, messaging) within banking applications. Leverage Kandy's WebRTC and SIP trunking capabilities with pre-built compliance templates for SOX, GLBA, and PCI-DSS requirements. Estimated TAM expansion of $8-12M in new ARR.

opportunities.title: Cross-Sell Kandy Messaging API to Existing AT&T Enterprise Customers
opportunities.description: Introduce CPaaS messaging (SMS, MMS, RCS, WhatsApp Business) to current AT&T enterprise base managing SIP trunking and voice. Bundle Kandy messaging APIs with existing telecom services contracts. Conservative penetration of 15-20% of installed base projects $1.5-2.2M incremental ARR within 18 months.
